items.question: Why would I use a glass mousepad?
items.answer: Glass mousepads offer truly unparalleled surface experiences and performance, whether you prefer speed or control. While maintaining their quickness for an incredibly long time. Since it’s hardened glass, the consistency of the surface will be unmatched, making it stand the test of time with significantly longer lifespan than cloth.

items.question: Is the surface coated?
items.answer: No. The texture is etched into the glass itself, not applied on top. Coatings wear through where you use them most, which is how a pad ends up feeling different in the middle than at the edges. Uncoated glass doesn't do that. What it feels like out of the box is what it feels like in two years

items.question: Are glass mousepads fragile?
items.answer: Our mousepads are built using tempered glass, making them extremely resistant to cracks, chips and long-term wear. Even though we’ve made the glass thinner for ergonomics, it's stil made of tough, tempered glass. The surface is also stain-proof and immune to issues like edge fraying or humidity damage.

props.body:

props.body:

items.question: Why should I use a gaming sleeve?
items.answer: Bare skin sticks. Your forearm drags on the pad and on the table edge, and that drag works against every movement your arm makes. A sleeve puts low-friction fabric between the two so your arm moves as freely as your mouse does. It's standard kit on stage at tournaments for exactly this reason.

items.question: Can I wear it on either arm?
items.answer: Yes. There's no left or right version, so one sleeve works on whichever arm you want it on, whether you are right handed or left handed.

items.question: Will it slide down during a long session?
items.answer: The top cuff is a grippy silicone band that holds at the bicep, and at 180gsm the fabric keeps its shape instead of loosening as it warms up. Lighter sleeves stretch out over a few hours and start creeping down the arm. Get the bicep measurement right from the size chart and this one stays where you put it.

props.body: The WALLHACK Pro Sleeve comes in 2 versions: a classic sleeve and a gloved variant.
props.heading: Classic or Glove

props.description: Straight cut, bicep to wrist. The low-friction fabric covers the part of your forearm that rests on the pad and stops there. Pick Classic if only your arm makes contact, or you just don't want anything past your wrist.
props.name: Classic

props.description: Same fabric, carried over the wrist to cover part of the palm and thumb. The cut is low-profile so it stays clear of your mouse, and the inner-thumb seam is stitched flat. Pick Glove if the side of your palm drags on the pad, or you want the glide to continue all the way to your grip.
props.name: glove

props.body: Drop artwork doesn't stop at the pad. Many releases ship a matching Pro Sleeve alongside the glass pad. Ghost in the Shell '95, EVANGELION, Miku OS, Awakening Sora, Frenzy Sora, Futurefall and more.

items.question: Why would I use mouse skates?
items.answer: Skates are the only part of your mouse that touches the pad, so they decide how it feels to move. Stock feet wear down and can't be adjusted. The difference is biggest on glass and other hard pads.

items.question: What mouse can I use mouse skates with?
items.answer: Almost any. Our skates aren't cut to a specific model. They go where your existing feet sit and flex to whatever base layout your mouse has. A dot set contains 40 pieces and a pill set 24, so there's enough for more than one mouse, or to try a few layouts before settling on one. Remove the stock feet first. The adhesive comes off clean, so nothing you try leaves a mark.

items.question: How often should I replace my skates?
items.answer: There's no set interval. It depends on your pad, how hard you press, and how much you play. Watch for the glide slowing down, or the mouse starting to wobble instead of sitting flat. Both mean the contact surface has worn unevenly. Swap them then. The old ones lift off residue-free, so there's nothing to clean up

props.body: The choice between PTFE and UHMWPE mouse skates ultimately comes down to personal preference. If ultra-low friction and a buttery smooth glide are top priorities, PTFE might be the preferred option. On the other hand, if durability and low-friction performance are crucial, UHMWPE mouse skates are a solid choice.
props.heading: choose your friction

props.description: Polytetrafluoroethylene, commonly known as PTFE, is a synthetic fluoropolymer of tetrafluoroethylene. PTFE is well-known for its low friction properties, making it an ideal material for mouse skates. The smooth surface of PTFE allows the mouse to glide effortlessly across the mouse pad, reducing friction and providing a more responsive feel.
props.name: PTFE

props.description: UHMW-PE mouse skates provide a controlled glide experience along with a high level of robustness. The material’s high molecular weight contributes to its excellent wear resistance, ensuring that the skates maintain their smooth glide even after prolonged use. Gamers who prefer a combination of control and durability often opt for UHMW-PE mouse skates.
props.name: UHMW-PE

props.body:
WALLHACK PTFE skates are available in a silent variant.
Silent Skates are the standard skates with a 0.15mm PU foam layer between the skate and your mouse. Most of the noise a mouse makes on glass isn't the skate sliding, it's vibration travelling up through the shell and out as sound. The foam sits in that path and absorbs it before it gets there.
props.heading: silent skates

props.body: Go Dot for a smaller footprint and the lowest possible contact area, or Pill for a larger pad that spreads pressure and adds a touch more control underhand.
props.heading: shape

props.description: Dots keep the contact patch as small as it goes. Each one is 7mm across, so there's less material touching the pad and less friction to work against. They're also the adjustable shape: you tune the feel dot by dot, adding one for more control or pulling one for more speed. A 2x2 or 3x3 layout is the usual starting point. Pick Dots if you want the fastest glide and the freedom to dial it in.
props.name: dots

props.description: A Pill is 14x7mm, roughly double a Dot, so it takes fewer of them to reach the same level of control. The larger footprint spreads the load. Your mouse sits flatter, sinks less into softer pads, and the skates wear down more slowly under pressure. Long swipes stay planted and predictable. Pick Pills if you want stability and longevity over outright top speed, or you'd rather fit them once and forget about them.
props.name: pills

props.body: Peel, wipe, stick. Fits most mouse shapes and comes off residue-free.

items.question: Why would I use a glass mousepad?
items.answer: Glass mousepads offer truly unparalleled surface experiences and performance, whether you prefer speed or control. While maintaining their quickness for an incredibly long time. Since it’s hardened glass, the consistency of the surface will be unmatched, making it stand the test of time with significantly longer lifespan than cloth.

items.question: Is the surface coated?
items.answer: No. The texture is etched into the glass itself, not applied on top. Coatings wear through where you use them most, which is how a pad ends up feeling different in the middle than at the edges. Uncoated glass doesn't do that. What it feels like out of the box is what it feels like in two years

items.question: Are glass mousepads fragile?
items.answer: Our mousepads are built using tempered glass, making them extremely resistant to cracks, chips and long-term wear. Even though we’ve made the glass thinner for ergonomics, it's stil made of tough, tempered glass. The surface is also stain-proof and immune to issues like edge fraying or humidity damage.

props.body:
Glass is the fastest and most consistent surface you can play on. The friction under your skates is identical every session, so the muscle memory you built last month still applies today.
The SP and CR are two of the most refined glass surfaces available, one tuned to run fast and one tuned to stop hard, both built so the pad is the last variable you have to think about.
props.heading: Why glass

props.body: The choice between the SP-005 and the CR-005 ultimately comes down to play style, type of game and preference of feel. Both pads are the same tempered glass. What differs is the etch, and what that does at the end of a movement. One surface lets the mouse run, the other gives you something to push against when you stop. The right one depends on whether your aim is built on tracking movements or flicking fast.
props.heading: choose your friction

props.description: The faster of the two. A slight texture gives you enough feedback to feel where the mouse is without slowing it down, which puts it in the middle of the range rather than at either extreme. Pick it if you prefer a low-friction, fast mouse gilde.
props.name: SP-005

props.description: The control surface. Press harder and it responds, slowing the glide instead of letting the mouse carry past the target. It's the closest thing we make to a cloth pad's stopping power, which makes it the straightforward choice if you're moving over from cloth and don't want to relearn how you aim.
props.name: CR-005

props.body:
Three layers, 3.3mm in total. The top is tempered glass, micro-etched so the texture is cut into the surface rather than applied to it, and left uncoated so there's nothing to wear through.
The color is printed on the underside, where your mouse never reaches it.
The bottom is 60A silicone running the full width of the pad, so the glass is supported across its whole area and grips the desk instead of resting on it.
props.heading: precision in every detail

props.body: The SP-005 edge goes through a three-step CNC machining process to produce a gradual taper. It's there for one reason: a hard edge under a forearm becomes a pressure point over a long session, and a sloped one doesn't. The refinement over the SP-004 edge is small on paper but obvious after an hour.
props.heading: Spill it, wipe it, keep playing

props.body: Glass is non-porous, and so is the silicone under it. Sweat, condensation, a knocked-over drink: none of it soaks in. Cleaning involves just a microfibre cloth and water, or a glass-safe cleaner if something has dried on. No stains, no edge fraying, no soft patches where your palm sits.
props.heading: Spill it, wipe it, keep playing

props.body:
Tempered glass isn't window glass. Tempered glass resists flexing, takes knocks that would crack an untreated sheet, and is built to hold together rather than shatter.Whether you're a casual user or a gaming enthusiast, the 005 generation guarantees a surface that lasts.
Not only is the 005 generation capable of withstanding drops. Now, you’ll never have to worry about your glass pad shattering or chipping in the mail, or when taking it to LAN parties, or even objects like your microphone falling onto it.
props.heading: durable

props.body: The SP-005 is available in a solid black and solid white color way.
props.heading: Black or white

props.body: The SP-005 doubles as a canvas. We work with artists and studios on limited runs, printed under the glass. Alongside original work. The pad underneath is the standard SP-005, unchanged.
props.heading: custom drops

props.body: The SP-005 and the CR-005 both ship in rugged plastic carrying cases designed to protect your pad on it’s journey to you, and wherever you decide to bring it.
props.heading: packaging

props.body: The pad is one part of it. We also make the M-001 mouse and the K-001 keyboard, all built to the same standard and designed to sit on a desk together. Matching materials, matching finishes, nothing that clashes.
props.heading: the perfect setup
